newsitem.title: USA: Bond firms donated to Jacksonville campaigns - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bond firms donated to Jacksonville campaigns - paper.

text.p: Two Duval County School Board members received nearly $8,000 of campaign contributions in 1992 from people and firms involved in a school bond deal, Florida Times-Union reported Wednesday.
The newspaper said the board members, Stan Jordan and Billy Parker, denied steering any business to the firms.

The Securities and Exchange Commission has subpoenaed their campaign records, as well as documents related to a 1992 school board bond refinancing. Lazard Freres & Co, which left most of the municipal bond business in December 1995, was the lead underwriter for the $184.5 million deal.
SEC officials declined to comment on the probe. Officials at Lazard headquarters in New York were not immediately available for comment.
The newspaper said the subpoenaes are part of a larger probe believed to focus on whether bond firms used political influence to win government contracts.
Times-Union said people associated with Lazard Freres donated $4,500 to Jordan's and Parker's campaigns in 1992.

A Tallahassee lobbyist who represented Lazard Freres in the deal, Nat Cole, also donated to the campaigns, the newspaper said. Cole's firm and family gave $2,000 to Jordan's 1992 campaign and $1,000 to Parker's, the newspaper said.
Jordan said he did not talk to Cole before the school board voted to award the contract to Lazard Freres.
Parker, described by the paper as a close friend of Cole, said he talked with Cole but that it did not influence his decision.
"I said, 'If you're the lowest bidder, I will vote for your company,'" Parker told the newspaper.
Although school board staff ranked Lazard eighth among firms seeking the deal, Jordan said Lazard was chosen because it charged the lowest fees.
The newspaper said associates of a printing firm that was paid $50,000 for printing the refunding bond documents also gave $1,960 to Jordan's campaign in 1992.

Additionally, Jordan's campaign received $500 in 1992 from William R. Hough & Co, which was the board's financial adviser for the bond refunding, the newspaper said. And two attorneys and a law firm that worked on the deal gave Parker's campaign $1,000, the newspaper said.
Robb Hough Jr, president of William R. Hough & Co, told Reuters in a telephone interview that the firm had been subpoenaed by the SEC and that "we intend to cooperate fully with them."
He said the firm's involvement in the deals related to the subpoenae "were totally legal and ethical."

The contributions occurred before the adoption of MSRB rule G-37, which bars firms from doing business with government agencies for two years if they have made campaign contributions to officials with the agency.

In addition to the school board documents, the SEC also subpoenaed documents related to three series of bonds issued by the Jacksonville Electric Authority in the early 1990s, while Lazard was its financial adviser.
Clyde Montgomery, a spokesman for the authority, confirmed the SEC had subpoenaed authority documents. But he told Reuters, "We have no idea of what the focus of the investigation is."
